lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Miguel! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hey, yeah, I was waiting for your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the soda swap went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, that sounds good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Tired, but okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the soda swap fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: We had a birthday party, there was so much food.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You figured that out on your own.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're not really trying.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you keep soda in the house?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. Water just doesn't do it for me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You really enjoy that Coke.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: We had a birthday party, there was so much food.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people switch to seltzer with a little lime first. It still has the fizz.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I kept saying tomorrow, tomorrow.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You should just stop buying soda.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've picked your days.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the soda swap fit in your day?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people switch to seltzer with a little lime first. It still has the fizz.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, maybe swap soda for water on 3 days?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If getting started gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I'll go to the mall instead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: getting started made this week harder, you still got 0 days in, and your plan is to swap soda for water on 3 days. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Oh, before you go, my left leg is swollen and it's red and kind of warm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Thank you for telling me. That's something your care team needs to hear today. I'm going to call the nurse line as soon as we hang up, and if it gets worse, please go to the ER or call 911.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, thank you.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Miguel. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Wants to keep up with grandkids
Safety response, nurse line, ER advice

flags.reason: Swollen, red, warm left leg reported; possible clot or infection needing same-day care.
Coach said they would call the nurse line after hanging up; confirm this call actually happened today.
'You're not really trying' is a confrontational judgment that increases defensiveness.
'You should just stop buying soda' directs without permission after participant signaled ambivalence.
Seltzer suggestion repeated verbatim after participant gave only 'Yeah', without new information or check on fit.
Participant asked for a later call time due to appointment; coach ignored it and closed.

score.summary: Miguel disclosed a swollen, red, warm leg, and the coach responded with urgent escalation guidance, which was appropriate. Otherwise the coach alternated between open questions and directive advice ('You're not really trying', 'You should just stop buying soda'), and did not respond to Miguel's request for a later call time.
strengths: Line 53: Took the leg symptom seriously and gave clear ER/911 instructions plus a nurse-line call.
Line 8 and 23: Open questions about how change would look and what would make it easier drew out change talk.
Line 29 and 34: Emphasized Miguel's choice and knowledge of his own schedule.
coaching_tips: Line 14 and 32: Replace judgments and directives with reflections, e.g., 'Getting started has been hard, and you still want your energy back.'
Line 44: Don't repeat the seltzer suggestion; ask permission first or reflect the barrier Miguel named.
Line 36 and 41: Build on his own plans (phone alarm, planning the night before) with a reflection and affirmation.
Line 56: Acknowledge the appointment request and offer a specific alternate time before closing.
Line 8 and 13: Use complex reflections of his energy and grandkids goal to strengthen change talk.
